name: popsicle
headline: Spotify Data Analysis: SQL Queries & Optimization
short_description: SQL for Music Streaming Analysis: A Hands-On Approach to Spotify User Engagement. Master key SQL queries to explore Spotify’s user behavior, identify listening trends, and optimize engagement. delivering data-driven insights for better content and marketing strategies.
author: jayantibhanushali007

sections.overview:
This skill teaches SQL analysis of Spotify datasets containing track attributes, artist information, and streaming metrics. It covers data exploration, query writing at beginner through advanced levels, and performance optimization techniques like indexing and execution plan analysis. The skill progresses through 15 practical questions addressing track filtering, aggregation, grouping, platform comparisons, and ranking tasks. You'll work with audio features such as danceability, energy, acousticness, and tempo alongside engagement metrics like streams, views, and comments. This approach helps developers and analysts extract actionable insights from music streaming data and build proficiency in production-grade SQL techniques.
Identifying top-performing tracks by streams, views, and engagement across platforms
Analyzing audio feature patterns to understand listener preferences by album or artist
Comparing streaming performance between Spotify, YouTube, and Apple Music
Calculating aggregate metrics like average danceability or total comments per album
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/jayantibhanushali007/Spotify_Data_Analysis_SQL`
sections.usage:
```
I want to analyze Spotify user engagement data using SQL. I have a dataset with user listening history, including track IDs, timestamps, and user IDs. Write SQL queries to help me identify top tracks, user listening patterns, and trends over time. Focus on [COMPANY] in the [INDUSTRY] sector. Provide queries for the following: 1) Top 10 most streamed tracks in the last 30 days, 2) User listening patterns by time of day, 3) Trends in user engagement over the past year.
```
